Toyota Sienna Buyer's Guide

The last V6 Siennas are quick and simple; the hybrids use about 40% less fuel. Which minivan to buy used, and the sliding door and seat recalls to check.

By Margot Devries · 4 chapters, about 15 min in all · Updated November 16, 2026 · Find one for sale

In this guide
  1. ●Overview
  2. 12017–2020
  3. 22021–2026
  4. 3V6 or hybrid
  5. 4Used checklist

The Sienna is Toyota's minivan, built in Princeton, Indiana, and it covers 2 very different generations in this guide. The 2017–2020 cars are the end of the third generation, with a 296-hp V6, an 8-speed automatic and, for years, the only all-wheel drive in the minivan class. The 2021 redesign made every Sienna a hybrid: 245 hp, all-wheel drive from a rear electric motor, and an EPA rating of 36 mpg combined, against 21 or 22 for the V6.

For a used buyer, the choice of generation is mostly a choice between power and fuel economy, with seating and recalls close behind. This guide has 4 chapters: one for each generation, one on choosing between the V6 and the hybrid, and the checklist to use before you buy.

Quick picks

  • Best all-rounder: a 2021 or later Sienna XLE, rated at 36 mpg combined with front-wheel drive.
  • Best value: a documented 2019–2020 Sienna LE or XLE, with Apple CarPlay as standard and the newer V6.
  • Most luxury: a 2021 or later Limited or Platinum, or a 2025 or later Platinum with the built-in vacuum and fridge.
  • Best in snow: any all-wheel-drive Sienna. The hybrid's system costs less fuel than the V6's.
  • Most flexible cargo space: a 2017–2020 car, whose second-row seats come out.
  • Think twice if you need to remove the second row. On the hybrid, the captain's chairs have built-in airbags and stay put.

The chapters

Chapter 1The Fastest Minivan of Its Day2017–2020 · Third generation · V6, front drive or AWD

A 296-hp V6, an 8-speed automatic and all-wheel drive no rival offered. The last of the gas Siennas is quick, roomy and simple to own.

3 min readChapter 2The Minivan That Went All-Hybrid2021–2026 · Fourth generation · Hybrid only, FWD or AWD

36 mpg from an 8-seat van, with all-wheel drive on every grade. The catches are a second row that stays put, and a run of seat recalls to confirm.

4 min readChapter 3Quicker or 40% Less Fuel2017–2026 · V6 or hybrid · FWD or AWD

The V6 is quicker and its seats come out. The hybrid uses about 40% less fuel and comes with a newer warranty. Here's how to choose, with the numbers.

3 min readChapter 4Check the Doors and the Seats2017–2026 · The used Sienna checklist

Family vans work hard, and the Sienna's weak spots are the parts families use most. How to check the one in front of you, and the recalls to confirm.
